rationale: Cysteine contains a thiol group and is central to many redox-regulated protein mechanisms, including reversible oxidation and oxidative stress-associated protein regulation.
interpretation_boundary: Sequence-level presence or clustering of cysteine does not prove oxidation, redox activity, solvent exposure, or functional modification.

rationale: Histidine contains an imidazole side chain and can participate in catalysis, metal coordination, and context-dependent oxidative or electrophile-associated modification biology.
interpretation_boundary: Sequence-level presence or clustering of histidine does not prove oxidation, electrophile adduction, structural exposure, or functional relevance.

rationale: Lysine contains a nucleophilic amine group and is relevant to carbonyl and lipid electrophile-associated protein adduction contexts under appropriate biochemical conditions.
interpretation_boundary: Sequence-level presence or clustering of lysine does not prove electrophile adduction, biochemical reactivity, or functional perturbation.
